primary_sources.title: Zotero linked and stored attachments
primary_sources.locator: Stored Files; Linked Files; Adding linked files
primary_sources.governing_context: Stored imports copy bytes; linked references retain external originals. Linked originals are neither synchronized nor deleted with the reference. Base-directory mapping is conditional on matching local trees.

primary_sources.title: Zotero missing linked file
primary_sources.version_context: Living support page, older recovery guidance
primary_sources.governing_context: External moves/deletion, incorrect base-directory mapping and external transfer lag are distinct causes. Locate changes a reference deliberately.

primary_sources.title: Zotero attachment operations
primary_sources.observed_operation: Read exact public source; no execution
primary_sources.governing_context: Separate imported and linked modes; linkFromFile creates a linked record. Relative linking stores attachments: plus the suffix, permits unresolved references, and indexes only with a resolvable base and existing target.

primary_sources.title: Zotero relocation proposal #2084
primary_sources.governing_context: The issue proposes bounded suffix search under a configured base and confirmation for one or several repairs. Issue closure alone does not establish shipped behavior.

primary_sources.title: Zotero 7.0 release history
primary_sources.locator: Nearest release headings around auto-relink and invalid-relative-path entries
primary_sources.governing_context: The potential auto-relink error fix belongs to 7.0.7, not the control map's 7.0.8. The invalid relative-path/base-directory entry belongs to 7.0.16.

primary_sources.title: Zotero relink UI
primary_sources.governing_context: UI discloses old/new paths and gives relink, cancellation and manual-location choices. Strings are corroborated by the caller, rather than treated as the matching algorithm.

primary_sources.title: Zotero relink caller
primary_sources.governing_context: Candidate construction and user dialog precede committed relink. The caller corroborates the limited UI-source claim.

primary_sources.title: Zotero relative-link tests
primary_sources.observed_operation: Inspected relevant upstream tests; no execution
primary_sources.governing_context: Tests cover absent base, existing and missing targets, conditional indexing and absolute-path rejection. Reading tests supplies context; no test was executed or credited as a candidate witness.

primary_sources.title: Final Cut Pro relinking
primary_sources.version_context: Living guide URL token is not an application release number
primary_sources.locator: Procedure steps 5-8; media requirements and non-undoable command
primary_sources.governing_context: Filename/proximity candidates undergo media-attribute analysis; users can remove bad matches and commit with Relink Files. Its media constraints and lack of undo are product-specific.

primary_sources.title: NSURL bookmarks and security scope
primary_sources.version_context: Living Foundation reference; bookmarks from macOS 10.6; security-scoped bookmarks from 10.7.3
primary_sources.locator: Bookmarks and Security Scope; Security-Scoped URLs
primary_sources.observed_operation: Retrieved official Markdown after web HTML/Markdown fetch limitations
primary_sources.governing_context: Bookmark relocation continuity is usual, not guaranteed. Persistent sandbox access needs resolution and balanced successful start/stop calls. A string path does not carry the URL security scope.

primary_sources.title: Apple sandbox access
primary_sources.version_context: Living macOS documentation; application entitlements/distribution remain owner facts
primary_sources.observed_operation: Read official Markdown and surrounding access conditions
primary_sources.governing_context: Document-relative bookmarks can be stored with an owning project and resolved by a process able to access it. Scoped bookmarks require access calls and stale-data replacement; ordinary OS permissions can still deny access.

primary_sources.title: Apple bookmark resolution
primary_sources.version_context: macOS method from 10.6; scoped support from 10.7.3
primary_sources.governing_context: App scope uses nil relativeURL; document scope uses the absolute owning-document URL. Unlocated/unmountable targets fail; last-known bookmark metadata may aid recovery.

primary_sources.title: Apple file resource identifier
primary_sources.governing_context: Equality applies to same path or same inode on one filesystem. This value is not persistent across system restart.

primary_sources.title: Windows FILE_ID_INFO
primary_sources.version_context: Learn updated 2024-02-22; requirements table lists Server 2012 and no supported client
primary_sources.locator: Structure, FileId member, requirements; related BY_HANDLE context
primary_sources.governing_context: Volume serial plus 128-bit ID compares open handles on one computer. This neither locates a moved file nor supplies permanent cross-machine identity. Target-client support needs an owner/version check.

primary_sources.title: Windows BY_HANDLE_FILE_INFORMATION
primary_sources.governing_context: IDs are filesystem-dependent and can be reused; FAT rename/defragmentation caveats apply. NTFS replacement has distinct semantics; the 64-bit field is insufficient for ReFS identity. Timestamps have filesystem-specific precision.

primary_sources.title: Linux inode
primary_sources.observed_operation: Read indexed primary manual; independently read exact release member after direct HTML timeouts
primary_sources.governing_context: Device/inode comparison is filesystem-scoped. Equal inode numbers can occur on different filesystems; no portable attachment identity follows from the number.

primary_sources.title: Linux opaque file handles
primary_sources.locator: Handle flags, permission, errors, notes and example context
primary_sources.observed_operation: Read indexed primary manual and exact release member
primary_sources.governing_context: Handle support varies; reopening requires CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH and can fail ESTALE. Unprivileged handle-generation/comparison and privileged reopening are distinct capabilities.

primary_sources.title: XDG Documents portal
primary_sources.locator: Overview; Add/AddFull; permissions; Delete; host paths
primary_sources.governing_context: Portal IDs name per-user access entries under the document mount. Persistence is explicit; deleting an entry does not delete source bytes. Grants and host-path access have caller restrictions.

primary_sources.title: RFC 8089
primary_sources.version_context: Standards Track, February 2017; published syntax, not a filesystem identity standard
primary_sources.governing_context: File URIs encode locations with platform/encoding differences. Non-local access and privilege handling require care. The locator-versus-identity conclusion is an engineering inference from the defined representation.

primary_sources.title: SQLite transactions
primary_sources.version_context: Living page updated 2026-02-18; target library version unspecified
primary_sources.locator: Sections 2.1-2.3; read snapshots, write upgrades and errors
primary_sources.governing_context: Multiple readers coexist with one simultaneous writer. Historic read snapshots and SQLITE_BUSY require application handling. Atomicity alone does not detect stale-window overwrite.

primary_sources.title: SQLite WAL
primary_sources.version_context: Living documentation; WAL from 3.7.0; 2026 WAL-reset fix context
primary_sources.governing_context: WAL requires same-host access and has one writer. A rare corruption race affects 3.7.0-3.51.2 with concurrent write/checkpoint activity from multiple connections; 3.51.3+ and named backports contain the fix.

primary_sources.title: SQLite WAL-reset fix release
primary_sources.governing_context: The official release records correction of the WAL-reset corruption bug. This corroborates the version gate, without establishing the notebook's selected backend or installed version.

primary_sources.title: Windows naming rules
primary_sources.locator: File/directory names; roots, namespace, length and case behavior
primary_sources.governing_context: Drive and UNC roots, component restrictions and case behavior vary. Lossless native path storage and filesystem-aware comparison are justified.

primary_sources.title: Apple APFS FAQ
primary_sources.version_context: Archived High Sierra/iOS 11-era guide, not a current target-matrix guarantee
primary_sources.governing_context: macOS APFS has case-sensitive and case-insensitive variants; archived documentation also describes normalization-insensitivity. A universal case-fold/normalization rule is inappropriate.

primary_sources.title: Apple symlink resolution
primary_sources.governing_context: Broken/unresolvable links can remain in the result; file URLs only. This helper alone does not certify containment, alias semantics or race-free traversal.

primary_sources.title: Linux realpath
primary_sources.observed_operation: Read indexed manual and exact release member
primary_sources.governing_context: Success expands links/dot components into a canonical absolute path; denied, missing and loop cases can fail. String resolution is not a race-free containment proof.

primary_sources.title: Windows final handle path
primary_sources.locator: Flags, final path, SMB normalized-component caveat
primary_sources.governing_context: The API resolves an open handle's final path. SMB normalized queries can fail when a component is inaccessible; returned volume-name form depends on flags.

primary_sources.title: Windows reparse points
primary_sources.governing_context: Filters/tags mediate reparse opens; mounted folders and links can redirect a lexical path. Unsupported filters can make open fail.

primary_sources.title: Windows symbolic links
primary_sources.governing_context: A link entry and its target are distinct; transparent traversal motivates explicit target/containment semantics.

primary_sources.title: Apple FSEvents
primary_sources.governing_context: Coalesced events need subtree rescans; dropped events need a full monitored-scope rescan; root changes need reconciliation. Current target SDK details remain implementation work.

primary_sources.title: Windows ReadDirectoryChangesW
primary_sources.locator: bWatchSubtree; overflow/zero bytes; ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR; network conditions
primary_sources.governing_context: Monitoring scope is selected by the caller. Overflow can discard the buffer; enumeration recovers state. Redirector/filesystem support and network buffer size constrain use.

primary_sources.title: Linux inotify
primary_sources.locator: Limitations, overflow/unmount, rename pairs and historical bugs
primary_sources.observed_operation: Read indexed primary content and exact release member, including surrounding rename/history context
primary_sources.governing_context: Directory watches are nonrecursive; queues drop events; remote changes are not reported; unmount removes watches; rename pairing is racy and can omit a destination.
